answer: Operator-Linked Cooldown Forge: each new wallet must wait out a per-operator cooldown before its first payout, and the cooldown duration is stored against the operator’s payout address, not the wallet. Rotating wallets gains nothing because the clock only advances when a payout clears through that address. An attacker running N identities through one operator pays N times the cooldown latency, and a glacier of queued payouts stalls throughput until the operator is forced to harbor each wallet under a distinct, separately aged address, multiplying their real setup cost per identity.
